Steps now fill the space as a row-major multi-column grid, modeled on standard TUI grid pickers. Research (ratatui docs, tui-widget-list, popular apps) pointed to row-major cells with directional navigation as the common pattern. Implementation: EditorState gains steps_columns (default 1, so all existing single-column tests/goldens stay byte-identical); the run loop derives columns each frame from terminal width via steps_columns_for_width (cell = widest filtered step + 9, clamped 1..=6) and App::set_steps_columns stores it. window_bounds is replaced by grid_window(index, len, columns, rows, scroll) which scrolls by one grid row and keeps pages column-aligned; steps_window/realign use it. Navigation: Up/Down/j/k move by columns (row stride), Left/Right/h/l move by one cell wrapping across rows; rendering lays cells left-to-right with row-local column padding and the cursor marker on the focused cell. Footer hint and editor help updated to '↑↓←→' / '↑↓←→ or hjkl'. Tests added: grid_window_scrolls_by_rows_in_multi_column_mode, steps_window_covers_columns_times_rows, vertical_movement_steps_by_columns, horizontal_movement_wraps_across_grid_rows, steps_columns_derive_from_width_and_widest_step, multi_column_steps_lay_out_cells_across_the_row, multi_column_grid_keeps_the_cursor_marker_on_the_focused_cell. just check green (230 lib tests); release binaries reinstalled. NOTE: README editor screenshot will need manual regeneration (vhs tapes) since the real TUI now renders multi-column at wide terminals.

The run log is now written to disk line by line: the stdout/stderr pump threads replace io::copy+BufWriter (flushed only at end-of-stream) with a pump_lines() read_until(newline) loop that writes and flushes the file after every line (terminal tee unchanged). This unblocks real-time tailing of a running profile — the TUI follow view polls the file every tick and now sees output as it happens instead of only after the run ends. Test: run_log_flushes_after_each_line uses a FlushCounter writer to prove exactly one flush per line plus complete content. just check green (229 lib tests).

Every column of the steps grid now lines up across rows: body_lines builds the whole cell matrix first, computes per-column widths (max cell width across all rendered rows), and pads each cell to its own column's width with the 2-space gap — instead of the previous row-local padding that let column boundaries drift whenever step names differed in length (only the first column looked aligned). Partial last-row cells render short. Test: multi_column_grid_aligns_every_column_across_rows uses ragged name lengths and asserts columns 2 and 3 start at identical offsets on both rendered rows. just check green (230 lib tests).

Run now opens the live log view immediately: run_now() sets View::Logs(LogsState::follow) at keypress instead of waiting for systemctl start to return, so the user lands on the log screen right away and x (stop) is reachable for the whole run — including while the start job is still in flight (systemd serializes the concurrent stop). pending_follow and run_after_result are deleted; the follow header now shows the real transitions (brief 'starting' while the start job runs -> 'running · elapsed' -> 'finished ok'/'FAILED'), and the footer spinner keeps the 'starting {name}' label honest. On start failure the error message shows and the log view header reports not-running. Tests: run_now_shows_loading_then_starts_the_service_through_the_manager now asserts the view opens before settle, and live_view_x_works_while_the_start_is_still_in_flight proves the stop reaches systemd mid-start. just check green (231 lib tests).

The follow view stops advertising 'esc background': the footer hint is now 'x stop  esc back  q quit' and the README describes r as opening the live view right away with output streaming in, x stopping, and esc going back while the dashboard badge keeps tracking the run (behavior unchanged — esc always returned and the run kept going). The live tail depth widens from 24 to 200 lines so j/k scrolling over the streaming log actually has context (scroll is preserved across ticks). Test renamed to live_view_escape_returns_and_run_keeps_going with updated assertion text. just check green (231 lib tests).

The schedule header is now just the category label 'schedule' (cyan, like steps/options) with no selected option after it — the current choice stays visible only on the 'preset: ...' row directly below, removing the 'schedule: daily' / 'preset: daily' duplication. Test asserts the header line carries no option and the preset row still shows the selection. just check green (231 lib tests).

Umbrella closed after the technical refinement was broken into and completing three sub-beads: topmatic-rhd (runner flushes the run log per line — the on-disk log is real-time, which was the root cause of the empty streaming view), topmatic-1re (run now opens the live log view immediately, pending_follow/run_after_result deleted, x stop reachable during the whole run including mid-start, header shows real starting -> running -> finished transitions), and topmatic-e0q ('esc background' framing removed from footer/README — esc is just back — and the live tail deepened to 200 lines for scroll context). Result: press r, land on the log screen instantly, watch output stream in as it happens, stop any time with x, esc always goes back. just check green (231 lib tests); commits 70350ce, 5bfda1f, 338cda5 + this one.

The linger help now explains itself in two terse bullets: '• linger — user timers survive logout' (what it does and why it matters for topmatic's user-level timers) followed by '• linger — loginctl enable/disable-linger' (how to control it, unchanged). Both bullets fit the <=48/<=62 width rules and avoid semicolons; help_explains_what_lingering_is_for asserts both explicit commands. just check green (231 lib tests).

Runs are now forensic by default: real (non-dry) invocations pass --run-type damp so topgrade prints each command as it executes (self-documenting logs, pairs naturally with the per-line flush and live view), and every invocation passes --log-filter info for step lifecycle beyond the default warn. --dry-run is never paired with --run-type (it IS run-type dry's alias); --show-skipped intentionally not adopted (useless with --only). Flag spellings captured from real 'topgrade --help' output, not invented. Tests: composes_config_dry_run_and_steps updated, dry_run_never_pairs_with_the_damp_run_type, real_runs_print_each_command_as_it_executes. just check green (233 lib tests).
